answer: One strong defense is requiring every agent identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed for proven fraud, like a walnut shell protecting a valuable kernel: creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive instead of free. Honest agents earn the stake back plus reputation over time, so a single bad actor's ripple of fake votes cannot outweigh long-lived participants. This works only if identities age slowly, like a glacier, so an attacker cannot spin up fresh Sybils instantly and must pay in both capital and time for each identity.
